The Volkswagen Golf GTI family

8 generations and variants in the Index, 1976–present. Oldest first; every card opens the full page, with its own versions, figures and story.

  1. 1976–1983

    Volkswagen Golf GTI (Mk1)

    The car that made the fast family hatchback a category of its own, plotted as an unofficial side project by a handful of Volkswagen staff. With 108 hp and only about 840 kg (1,850 lb) to carry, it could embarrass costlier sports cars and still handle the weekly shopping, and a planned run of 5,000 grew to 461,690.

    108 hp9.0 sec 0-60113 mph top461,690 built
  2. 1984–1992

    Volkswagen Golf GTI (Mk2)

    The GTI that went to the gym. Bigger, more solid and better built than the Mk1, it kept Giugiaro's lines under broader shoulders, gained a 16-valve engine in 1986, and is the shape many people picture when they hear the name.

    137 hp8.9 sec 0-60130 mph top66,223 built
    16-valve, Europe · 16-valve, US · 8-valve, US
  3. 1991–1997

    Volkswagen Golf GTI (Mk3)

    The heavy years. A 2.0-liter engine and a far better cabin, but more weight and softer manners left the Mk3 GTI behind the French hot hatches, and the VR6 Golf of the same era stole its thunder.

    148 hp8.8 sec 0-6028,115 built
    2.0 16-valve · 2.0 8-valve, US · VR6
  4. 1998–2004

    Volkswagen Golf GTI (Mk4)

    A beautifully made Golf wrapped around a GTI that couldn't justify its badge. The cabin set a standard the industry copied, the 1.8-liter turbo was quick but characterless, and the R32, the first production car offered with a dual-clutch gearbox, rescued the generation.

    148 hp7.3 sec 0-6060,995 built
    1.8-liter turbo · 2.8-liter VR6
  5. 2004–2009

    Volkswagen Golf GTI (Mk5)

    The GTI that won back the badge's good name after 2 forgettable generations. A turbocharged, direct-injected 2.0-liter 4-cylinder and, for the first time, a fully independent multi-link rear suspension made it comfortable, composed and properly quick again.

    197 hp7.2 sec 0-60146 mph top181,000 built
  6. 2009–2013

    Volkswagen Golf GTI (Mk6)

    Less a new car than a hard polish of the Mk5. More power, better damping, a quieter cabin and XDS, which brakes the inside front wheel to imitate a limited-slip differential, made it the GTI people buy when they want a Mk7 and can't afford one.

    207 hp6.1 sec 0-6063,016 built
  7. 2013–2020

    Volkswagen Golf GTI (Mk7)

    The peak, and everyone knows it. The MQB platform made it lighter than the car it replaced for the first time in 40 years, and the Performance version's electronically controlled limited-slip differential changed what a front-wheel-drive car could do.

    227 hp6.4 sec 0-60
  8. 2020–present

    Volkswagen Golf GTI (Mk8)

    The fast, frustrating present. Objectively the best-driving GTI yet, but the launch cabin's touch sliders angered owners. The Mk8.5 fixed most of it with 261 hp and a real volume knob, and the manual gearbox is gone.

    241 hp5.1 sec 0-60
